en.title: Minimum Remaining Stones After Exactly k Half-Pile Removals
en.description:
Each time, choose any pile and remove floor(stones/2) from it, leaving ceil(stones/2). The same pile may be chosen repeatedly. After exactly k operations, minimize the total number of remaining stones.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and numeric ranges missing from the original text are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n k, and the second line contains n pile sizes. Original constraints: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤pile size≤10000, 1≤k≤100000.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 12; 12; 2. The examples were checked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Use a max-heap of negated values: each time, take the largest pile, subtract half rounded down, and push back the half rounded up. Once the maximum is 1, further operations change nothing, so you can stop.
